title: Persisted anchor corpus and human-audit gate for batching/caching optimizer
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Build a persisted anchor prompt corpus and a human-audit gate that together validate automatic batching/caching recommendations before traffic-affecting applies. The goal is to catch subtle quality regressions introduced by more aggressive batching or cache prefix changes while preserving most cost wins from autotuning.
background: Existing autotuners produce configuration deltas (batch sizes, prefix reuse heuristics, cache TTL) that can reduce per-token cost but occasionally change model behaviour in ways not detected by token-level heuristics. We need an operationalizable harness combining deterministic anchor prompts, lightweight semantic metrics, and a fast human-audit step for borderline cases so that config applies can proceed automatically for low-risk changes and pause for manual review when needed.
tasks: Design anchor corpus schema and persistence format (metadata: intent, expected length, error tolerances)
Implement anchor runner in evaluation service to score candidate configs against persisted anchors
Create a lightweight semantic similarity metric: embedding cosine + normalized edit distance pipeline
Define pass/fail thresholds and delta windows for auto-apply vs human-audit
Wire human-audit UI in Console: show pairs, diff highlights, and accept/reject buttons
Integrate with autotuner: shadow-apply -> anchor-run -> auto-apply/human-gate -> rollout orchestration
Add monitoring dashboards and alerting rules for anchor failures and audit latency
Create PRD and run two-week internal trial with selected customers and internal services
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chose persisted anchor corpus over ephemeral golden prompts to ensure stable regression baselines across releases
2026-02-28: Metric design approved: hybridScore = 0.6 * embedding_cosine + 0.4 * normalized_levenshtein_sim
2026-03-03: Thresholds provisional: hybridScore drop > 0.02 triggers human-audit; drop > 0.05 triggers auto-pause/rollback
2026-03-07: Opted for progressive apply: small % traffic can auto-apply when hybridScore delta within 0.01 and cost saving > 10%
2026-03-09: Human-audit to be staffed by on-call SRE/ML engineer with 2-hour SLAs for triage
acceptance_criteria: Anchor runner executes against candidate config in < 90s for 500 anchors
Persisted anchor corpus contains >= 500 diverse prompts across 12 intent buckets
HybridScore computation is deterministic and reproducible between runs (max floating variance < 1e-6)
Auto-apply path allowed when: hybridScore median delta <= 0.01 AND cost reduction estimate >= 8%
Human-audit path triggers when: 0.01 < hybridScore median delta <= 0.05 OR cost reduction < 8% but operational risk flagged
Auto-pause and rollback occurs when hybridScore median delta > 0.05 OR any anchor falls below absolute hybridScore 0.75
Human audits completed within SLA 2 hours for 95% of cases during trial
Internal trial shows no customer-facing regression in A/B tests (preference swing <= 3% toward baseline)
test_plan: Unit tests for hybridScore computation with synthetic pairs (embedding fixtures + edit distances)
Integration tests: run anchor runner in CI against a known safe config and a deliberately regressed config; assert thresholds behave as expected
Shadow apply experiments: run autotuner on staging traffic, compute anchors, and compare to baseline outputs; record hybridScore deltas
Human-audit dry run: present 50 candidate regressions to reviewers and measure inter-rater agreement (Krippendorff alpha target >= 0.7)
Canary A/B: 5% traffic for 48 hours with monitoring on latency, token cost, user-facing error rate, and anchor deltas
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Persisted anchor corpus and anchor-runner enabled for internal services only (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (alpha): Enable auto-apply for low-risk deltas on selected customer tenants with full logging (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (beta): Expand to majority of hosted API, keep human-audit for medium-risk deltas (6 weeks)
Phase 3 (GA): Auto-apply defaults enabled, human-audit on-demand and for >threshold deltas; monitor and iterate
risks: Anchor corpus not representative -> false negatives (missed regressions)
Hybrid metric may overfit to anchors and not surface semantic drift on long-tail prompts
Human reviewers inconsistent -> noisy gating decisions
Added evaluation latency may slow down autotuner cadence and reduce cost wins
Operational complexity: more moving parts increases incident surface
mitigations: Maintain periodic corpus refresh cadence and automated sampling from live traffic for coverage
Add a long-tail sentinel: monitor user-reported regressions and attach offending prompts to corpus
Implement annotation UI with reviewer guidance and example verdicts to improve consistency
Allow autotuner to apply low-risk deltas in background while human audits run for medium-risk ones
Ship robust observability and runbook for debugging anchor runner failures
notes: Design review 2026-02-27: PM wants explicit cost deltas surfaced to auditors
SRE feedback 2026-03-04: ensure anchor runner can run in a preemptible worker pool
Security 2026-03-05: anchor corpus must be scrubbed for PII before persisting
